newsitem.title: USA: Rubin says U.S. dollar policy remains unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Rubin says U.S. dollar policy remains unchanged.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin repeated on Tuesday that U.S. dollar policy remains unchanged.
"Our policy with respect to the dollar remains the same as it always has," he told reporters following a speech to the U.S. Conference of Mayors.
Rubin declined comment on both the level of the dollar and its recent movements.
Japanese officials in recent days have suggested that they are uneasy with the recent steep drop of the dollar against the yen.
Rubin said that the Clinton administration has yet to decide when to seek congressional approval for fast-track negotiating authority for trade agreements.
"The decision has not yet been made," he said.
Fast-track authority would allow the administration to negotiate trade agreements that would then face an up or down vote in Congress without the threat of amendments by lawmakers.
The administration is considering whether to press Congress next month to grant such authority or wait until September.
Some administration officials have suggested delaying the request for fast-track authority to allow Congress to first debate the granting of Most Favored Nation trading status to china.
Rubin acknowledged that that was a consideration but stressed that no decision on the timing of a fast-track request has been made.
"They are both very important trading initiatives," Rubin said, referring to fast track and to China MFN. "We need to accomplish both."
President Clinton on Monday said he wants to renew Most Favored Nation trading privileges for China for another year. Congress has until Aug 31 to decide whether to try to overrule that decision.
